provenance: Decided by Claude at the user's request, not reviewed by the team (Practicum_Agent DECISIONS.md F1 rows 20 to 22). Every link is team judgment based on wording overlap between a Q12 item and a source's construct; no source names Q12.

evidence_strength_meaning.Stronger: Passes all four evidence checks: close match, workplace or field evidence, a performance or behavior outcome, and no contrary result among the linked findings.
evidence_strength_meaning.Moderate: Workplace or field evidence with a performance or behavior outcome, but either the match is partial or a linked finding points the other way.
evidence_strength_meaning.Limited: No workplace evidence, no performance or behavior outcome, or both a partial match and a contrary result.
evidence_strength_meaning.None: No research from our corpus yet.

plain_habits: Say exactly what a finished piece of work looks like

A.why: Role ambiguity, not knowing what is expected, is the Q01 construct (TI-D1-d)

B.why: Workplace and field studies (Gilboa 2008; Dossett 1980; Dirkmaat 2023)

C.why: Supervisor-rated and objective performance (TI-D1-d); group performance (TI-D1-c)

D.why: No linked card reports a contrary result

Q02.plain_label: Having the information and tools to do the work
plain_habits: Point people to the information, tools, or person who can help

A.why: Partial. Q02 covers materials and equipment as well as information; Tool 2's rubric also marks it partial

C.why: Lower performance with missing information and tools (TI-D4-d)

D.why: No linked card reports a contrary result

plain_habits: Praise the specific work, not the person

A.why: Positive feedback from the supervisor is recognition (PF-F1-c)

D.why: Kluger & DeNisi (1996) found weaker effects when feedback included praise (PF-F1-b)

plain_habits: Give a concrete next step for improving

A.why: Forward-looking developmental feedback is encouragement of development (PF-F4-c)

C.why: Supervisor-rated creativity, a rated work behavior, though not task performance (PF-F4-c limits)

D.why: No linked card reports a contrary result

Q07.plain_label: Asking for and acting on input
plain_habits: Ask the team for their input explicitly
Say what you will do with the input
Report back what was done with it, or why not

A.why: Managerial openness to input matches 'my opinions seem to count' (TD-C9-a, TD-C9-b)

C.why: Voice behavior (TD-C9-a) and observer-rated team performance (TD-C9-d)

D.why: Earlier survey studies found no link (Detert & Burris p.870); outcome evidence called limited (Morrison 2014)

A.why: Meaning-making language answers why the work is important (TI-D3-b)

C.why: Perception and trust only; no reliable performance link (TI-D3-a)

D.why: No linked card reports a contrary result

plain_habits: Set a check-in point when assigning work
Compare progress with the goal or the last result

A.why: Feedback on progress toward goals is the Q11 construct (TI-D5-a, PF-F3-a)

D.why: Alvero (2001) found feedback with goal setting less consistent than feedback alone (TI-D5-c limits)

checks.A: Match: the linked findings describe the construct the Q12 item asks about
checks.B: Setting: at least one linked finding comes from a workplace or field study
checks.C: Outcome: at least one linked finding reaches performance or rated work behavior, not only perception or trust
checks.D: Consistency: no linked card reports a contrary result

evidence_checklist.label_rule: Stronger = all four pass. Moderate = B and C pass and exactly one of A or D fails. Limited = B or C fails, or both A and D fail. None = no linked cards.
evidence_checklist.score: Tie-break score = number of checks passed (0 to 4). It only orders areas whose gaps are exactly equal; it never multiplies a gap.
evidence_checklist.provenance: Applied by Claude at the user's request 2026-11-07 (Practicum_Agent DECISIONS.md F1 row 26). Team judgment, not a research finding. Not reviewed by the team.
